slides.title:
The shoe everyone
called *ugly* built a
$4 billion company.

Three friends in their 40s,
on a Caribbean sailing trip,
bet on a *foam boat shoe*.
slides.sub:
Scott Seamans found the clog in Canada
(Foam Creations) and added a heel strap
(Quartr).

slides.title:
pairs at the Fort Lauderdale
boat show, Nov. 2002.
*All sold out*, at $30 each.
slides.sub:
Per Quartr. Footwear News says
the first batch was 200 pairs.
Either way: gone.

slides.title:
in sales in 2007.
46.9 million pairs.
*Up from $110M in 2005.*
slides.sub:
Feb. 2006: Nasdaq IPO, the largest
in footwear history (Quartr).

slides.title:
The stock by the end of 2008.
*Too many pairs,
too fast.*
slides.sub:
Inventory fears halved the share price
in two weeks in Nov. 2007. Losses in 2009,
profit again in 2010 (Quartr).

slides.title:
In 2006, Crocs buys *Jibbitz*:
little charms you clip
into the holes.
slides.sub:
Price: $10M, plus up to $10M more
if targets were hit. In 2024, Jibbitz made
over $260M, 6%+ of sales (Quartr).

slides.title:
Designer Christopher Kane
puts Crocs *on the runway*
in London. Balenciaga follows.
slides.sub:
Then Post Malone, Bad Bunny, KFC…
They didn't hide the "ugly".
They leaned in (Quartr).

slides.title: You love us or hate us – and that's OK because that means *you're paying attention* to us.
slides.author:
Michelle Poole
Crocs brand president, 2020-2024
(via Quartr)

slides.title:
Your weird
is *your marketing*.
slides.sub:
Crocs didn't fix the look. They sold it.
